comparisons.peer_topic: Derivative instruments hedging policy and status
comparisons.peer_summary: The company uses derivative financial instruments, specifically foreign exchange forward contracts and treasury rate locks, to manage exposure to foreign exchange and interest rate risks for hedging purposes, not for speculation. Outstanding derivatives are recognized at fair value based on Level 2 inputs. As of November 3, 2024, and October 29, 2023, the company had no material foreign exchange forward contracts outstanding. In August 2023, the company settled $5.5 billion in treasury rate lock contracts for a $371 million cumulative gain, with $75 million to be amortized to interest expense through October 2034 upon the issuance of $1.75 billion senior notes, and the remainder amortized for future debt.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom use foreign currency forward contracts that are not designated as accounting hedges to manage foreign exchange risk on monetary items, recognizing fair value changes in earnings rather than other comprehensive income. AMD explicitly states these contracts generally mature within 3 months and had a notional value of $642 million as of December 2024 with immaterial fair value. Broadcom also uses these non-designated forward contracts, recording changes in fair value in other income (expense), net, and reported no material contracts outstanding as of its November 2024 fiscal year-end, highlighting a difference in scale and materiality of the outstanding exposure.

sentences.text: The Company also enters into foreign currency forward contracts to reduce the short-term effects of foreign currency fluctuations on certain receivables or payables denominated in currencies other than the U.S. Dollar.
These forward contracts generally mature within 3 months and are not designated as accounting hedges.
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the notional value of these outstanding contracts was $642 million and $568 million, respectively.
The fair value of these contracts was not material as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.
We use foreign exchange forward contracts to manage exposure to foreign exchange risk.
These forward contracts are not designated as hedging instruments, and the changes in fair value are recognized in other income (expense), net in the period of change.
We did not have any material foreign exchange forward contracts outstanding as of November 3, 2024 or October 29, 2023.
The gains and losses recorded in other income (expense), net for derivative instruments not designated as hedges were not material.

comparisons.peer_topic: Non-designated hedging of monetary assets and debt investments
comparisons.peer_summary: Non-designated hedges employ foreign currency and interest rate contracts to economically hedge recognized monetary assets/liabilities and fixed-rate debt investments, with fair value changes recorded through earnings in related line items.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and AMD both utilize non-designated foreign currency contracts to economically hedge recognized monetary assets and liabilities. Intel describes this as hedging the functional currency equivalent cash flows of these items, with fair value changes recorded in earnings (primarily interest and other, net). AMD similarly uses non-designated forward contracts to reduce short-term effects of currency fluctuations on non-USD receivables or payables, also recording fair value changes through earnings. The key difference is that Intel's disclosure emphasizes the offset against underlying assets/liabilities in earnings, while AMD specifies the maturity (under 3 months) and provides specific notional values ($642 million).

sentences.text: The Company also enters into foreign currency forward contracts to reduce the short-term effects of foreign currency fluctuations on certain receivables or payables denominated in currencies other than the U.S. Dollar.
These forward contracts generally mature within 3 months and are not designated as accounting hedges.
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the notional value of these outstanding contracts was $642 million and $568 million, respectively.
The fair value of these contracts was not material as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023.

Non-designated hedges use foreign currency contracts to economically hedge the functional currency equivalent cash flows of recognized monetary assets and liabilities, and non-US-dollar-denominated debt instruments classified as hedged investments.
We also use interest rate contracts to hedge interest rate risk related to our US-dollar-denominated fixed-rate debt investments classified as hedged investments.

The change in fair value of non-designated derivatives is recorded through earnings in the line item on the Consolidated Statements of Operations to which the derivatives most closely relate, primarily in interest and other, net.
Changes in the fair value of the underlying assets and liabilities associated with the hedged risk are generally offset by the changes in the fair value of the related derivatives.
